title: SERENE Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Cognitive Control
official: Suicide-related Experience Reduction Via Enhancement of Neuroplasticity
summary:
SERENE is an experimental study evaluating low-intensity focused ultrasound neuromodulation of cognitive control circuitry in adults with a lifetime history of suicide attempt or suicidal ideation, but without current suicidality.

Participants will complete screening, cognitive control tasks, MRI/fMRI, ecological momentary assessments, and low-intensity focused ultrasound neuromodulation using the DIADEM system. The study will examine whether low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) neuromodulation changes cognitive control performance measured by the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) and EEG event-related spectral power in the alpha and theta frequency bands.

The study will also examine the time course of LIFU effects and explore whether changes in cognitive control circuitry relate to self-reported experiences, including mood, anxiety, psychosis symptoms, suicidal ideation, and emotion regulation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Lifetime history of suicide attempt or suicidal ideation, as determined by the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale
* Score in specified ranges on measures of cognitive control behavior and/or cognitive control circuit function
* No current suicide ideation or behavior within the past 3 months, as determined by the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale
* Age 18 to 65 years
* Speaks and understands English
* Primary user of a smartphone

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under age 18
* Neurological disorder that may affect fMRI scan results or cause reaction to LIFU to differ from healthy adults
* Regular use of psychoactive medication, except PRN use if the participant is willing and able to abstain during the study period
* Psychiatric hospitalization within the past 3 months
* Contraindication to fMRI scanning, including claustrophobia, unremovable piercings, pregnancy, medical devices such as pacemakers, or a movement or sleep disorder
* Pregnant or may have reason to believe they are pregnant
* Diagnosis of certain psychiatric conditions, such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or a developmental disorder other than ADHD
* Any other neurological, autoimmune, or medical disorder that may inhibit participation
* Children
* Pregnant women/persons
* Fetuses
* Neonates
* Prisoners
* Adults lacking capacity to consent or adults with diminished or fluctuating capacity to consent
* Non-English speakers
* Individuals unable to read
* Employees of the researcher
* Students of the researcher
* Individuals approached during a stressful situation, such as an emergency room setting or childbirth
* Individuals with fear of negative consequences for not participating
* Any other circumstance that could increase vulnerability to coercion or exploitation
